**CONTROLLED**

# B.1.4 KSI Mapping and Compensating-Control Architecture

<!-- Diagrams for this leaf are not yet produced; text and tables below are the
     complete content. A KSI-namespace map and a detect→register→compensate→
     evidence→transport pipeline diagram are natural additions once this leaf
     clears governance review. -->

## 1. Position

[B.1](B1-gcc-moderate-boundary-model.qmd) names the four NIST 800-53 controls
that constrain outbound telemetry (SI-4, AU-2, AU-3, SC-7) and the capability
dispositions those controls produce.
[B.1.1](B1-1-gcc-moderate-three-way-conflict.qmd) treats the resulting
mandate-level conflict. [B.1.3](B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd)
gives the agency-side rebuild plan. None of the three answers the two
questions an assessor or a 3PAO actually asks when the SSP cites a
compensating control: *which specific FedRAMP KSI control ID does this
satisfy*, and *what code produces the evidence*. This leaf answers both, and
in doing so it surfaces two reconciliation gaps in the substrate's own KSI
and gap-registry artifacts that were not previously documented anywhere in
the boundary series.

This leaf is deliberately narrower and more mechanical than its siblings. It
does not re-argue the boundary model; it walks the control-ID mapping and the
code path from a first-person, "here is exactly what runs and what it
proves" perspective.

## 2. Two KSI Namespaces That Are Not Interchangeable

The substrate carries two separately-maintained KSI rule corpora. Confusing
them — which is easy to do, since both use the `KSI-` prefix — produces
exactly the kind of unattributed claim the boundary-inference methodology in
[B.1 §2](B1-gcc-moderate-boundary-model.qmd) exists to prevent. Both paths
below are relative to the substrate's package root; both are linked under
their real locations in §9.

| | `rules/ksi/` | `ksi/rules/` |
|---|---|---|
| **ID shape** | NIST-family-keyed: `KSI-AC-02`, `KSI-SC-07`, `KSI-AU-06`, plus vendor sub-corpora `KSI-CARK-*` (CyberArk), `KSI-ORGTREE-*`, `KSI-RECIP-*` (HRIT reciprocity), `KSI-SNOW-*` (ServiceNow) | Sequential: `KSI-001` … `KSI-029` |
| **Count** | 191 rules (per `index.yaml` stats block) | 29 rules (verified by directory listing — see §4) |
| **Authority** | Substrate-native. Its own index explicitly disclaims official status, describing itself as keyed to NIST 800-53 families and stating plainly that it is *"not the official FedRAMP 20x KSI taxonomy."* | Mapped directly to the pinned, vendored **FedRAMP CR26** KSI catalog (theme-prefixed IDs like `KSI-IAM-ELP`, `KSI-MLA-LET`) |
| **Governing doc** | None — implicit in the rule files and the local-to-family cross-reference file (`control-to-ksi-mapping.yaml`) | [`UIAO_137`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-cr26-ksi-mapping.md) (this leaf's primary source) |
| **Consumer** | `models.fedramp`, KSI evaluation over SCuBA / substrate-native signals | `fedramp-cr26-catalog` conformance adapter (ADR-061 D3); emits `fedramp:ksi-mapping-source` props |

For a question of the shape *"does the SSP's KSI evidence trace to an
official FedRAMP 20x control?"* — the question a 3PAO asks — the second
corpus (`ksi/rules/`) is the relevant one, because it alone is
pinned to the official catalog. §3–§4 below cover it. The first corpus
(`rules/ksi/`) reappears in §5 as the namespace that the boundary
gap registry's `ksi_ids` field should — but mostly does not — resolve
against.

## 3. The CR26 Catalog Pin and What It Currently Covers

Per `UIAO_137 §2`, the mapping is pinned to a specific, hash-identified
snapshot of the FedRAMP CR26 (Consolidated Rules) catalog:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Snapshot SHA | `c31eb04c082d6d578a26a00de9a482707ab7a00c` |
| Catalog UUID | `092dc25a-18ca-51d9-ab85-744e5435405e` |
| KSI themes in catalog | 10 — KSI-CMT, KSI-CNA, KSI-CED, KSI-IAM, KSI-INR, KSI-MLA, KSI-PIY, KSI-RPL, KSI-SVC, KSI-SCR |
| KSI controls in catalog | 46 |

The `fedramp-cr26-catalog` adapter emits `DRIFT-PROVENANCE` if a CR26 ID
cited in the mapping no longer resolves against this pinned snapshot — so
the pin itself is continuously verified. What is **not** continuously
verified is whether the mapping's prose description of its own coverage
stays current as new local rules are added. §4 documents a concrete case
where it did not.

### 3.1 Coverage as of this leaf (verified against the live rule corpus)

`UIAO_137`'s body (last updated 2026-06-18) states 14 local rules
(`KSI-001`–`KSI-014`) covering 21 of 46 CR26 controls (~46%). A direct
listing of `ksi/rules/` and a grep of the machine-readable
companion (`adapters/fedramp_cr26_catalog/mappings/ksi-mapping.yaml`,
which the same document says "must stay in lockstep" with the prose) show
**29 rules** (`KSI-001`–`KSI-029`) mapping to **32 of 46** CR26 controls
(~70%):

| CR26 theme | Controls | Covered (documented, `UIAO_137` §4) | Covered (current, verified) | Gap closed by |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| KSI-IAM | 6 | 6/6 | 6/6 — unchanged | — |
| KSI-CMT | 4 | 4/4 (scaffold, not evaluable — ADR-111) | 4/4 (scaffold, not evaluable — ADR-111) | — |
| KSI-CED | 1 | 0/1 | **1/1** | `KSI-022` |
| KSI-INR | 3 | 0/3 | **3/3** | `KSI-023`, `KSI-024`, `KSI-025` |
| KSI-PIY | 5 | 0/5 | **5/5** | `KSI-017`–`KSI-021` |
| KSI-RPL | 4 | 0/4 | **4/4** | `KSI-026`–`KSI-029` |
| KSI-SCR | 2 | 0/2 | **2/2** | `KSI-015`, `KSI-016` |
| KSI-MLA | 5 | 2/5 | 2/5 — unchanged | — |
| KSI-CNA | 8 | 2/8 | 2/8 — unchanged | — |
| KSI-SVC | 8 | 3/8 | 3/8 — unchanged | — |
| **Total** | **46** | **21/46 (46%)** | **32/46 (70%)** | |

Every one of the five themes `UIAO_137 §4` flagged by name as having *"zero
local rules"* — KSI-CED, KSI-INR, KSI-PIY, KSI-RPL, KSI-SCR — is now fully
covered. The remaining true gap is 14 controls across three themes:
KSI-CNA (6 open), KSI-MLA (3 open), KSI-SVC (5 open) — plus the 4 KSI-CMT
controls that are mapped but not yet evaluable pending the CR26 VDR/VER
evidence contract (ADR-111).

## 4. Finding: `UIAO_137`'s Coverage Narrative Has Drifted From Its Own Rule Corpus

**RESOLVED 2026-08-06.** `UIAO_137` §2–§5 were regenerated against the
live rule corpus and the live CR26 catalog snapshot: the rule count now
reads 29 (not 14), coverage reads 32 of 46 (~70%, not 21 of 46), and the
"zero local rules" framing for KSI-CED/INR/PIY/RPL/SCR was replaced with
their actual (full) coverage. The finding below is preserved as the
record of what was found and why; it no longer describes the current
document.

This is a documentation-staleness finding, stated with the same load-bearing
honesty [B.1.3 §11](B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd) applies
to the rebuild-compensation ceiling.

`UIAO_137 §4` names five themes with explicit zero coverage and calls the
gap *"expected... downstream work"*. Fifteen rules exist today —
`KSI-015` through `KSI-029` — that close exactly those five themes, each
correctly mapped in the machine-readable companion
(`ksi-mapping.yaml`) to the precise CR26 control the prose said was missing
(e.g. `KSI-022 → KSI-CED-RAT`, `KSI-026 → KSI-RPL-ABO`). The rules and their
mapping entries are real, committed, and internally consistent with each
other. What has not been updated is `UIAO_137`'s own narrative text: its
"14 rules," "21 of 46," and its "zero local rules" framing for those five
themes in §2 and §4 no longer describe the repository.

This is exactly the class of drift the document's own machinery is designed
to catch for the *catalog* (`DRIFT-PROVENANCE` on a CR26 ID going stale) but
does not catch for the *document's self-description of its own coverage*,
because no automated check diffs `UIAO_137`'s prose tables against a live
count of `ksi/rules/*.yaml`. Recommended remediation: either
generate §3–§4 of `UIAO_137` from the same script that presumably produced
`ksi-mapping.yaml`'s coverage, or add a CI check that fails when the rule
count in `ksi/rules/` diverges from the count asserted in
`UIAO_137`'s frontmatter — the same discipline
[B.1.3's fix-coverage matrix](B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd#6-signal-by-signal-rebuild-coverage)
already applies via its `generate_rebuild_coverage.py` generator comment.

## 5. Finding: The Boundary Gap Registry's `ksi_ids` Field Does Not Reconcile Against Either KSI Namespace

**RESOLVED 2026-08-06.** Every `ksi_ids` value described below as
non-resolving or topically wrong has been corrected in
`gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml` against the `rules/ksi/` NIST-family
corpus, resolved from each gap's own `nist_controls` field — the same
derivation §7's "corrected trace" table below already worked out.
`GAP-ENT-001` was already correct and is unchanged. The registry's
summary block was also found to have drifted (undercounting `total_gaps`
as 15 against the actual 17 entries, and misclassifying `GAP-INT-006` as
unmitigated when its `status` is `COMPENSATED`) and was corrected in the
same pass. The finding below is preserved as the record of what was
found; it no longer describes the registry's current state.

`gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml` (ADR-033 §3; header states *"ATO artifact:
yes — feeds SSP Section 13"*) carries a `ksi_ids` array on every gap entry,
described in ADR-033 as *"Input to the continuous monitoring KSI signal
set"* and, in the ADR's implementation path, wired to *"Appendix T risk
scoring."* Checking those IDs against the two namespaces documented in §2–§4
surfaces a second reconciliation gap, distinct from and additional to §4's.

**Most `ksi_ids` values do not resolve to any file in either corpus.**
`ksi/rules/` tops out at `KSI-029`; `rules/ksi/` uses
family-prefixed IDs, not bare numbers. Values like `KSI-047`, `KSI-048`,
`KSI-062`, `KSI-063`, `KSI-071`, `KSI-087`, `KSI-098`, `KSI-099`, `KSI-112`,
and `KSI-113` — cited across `GAP-INT-001`, `GAP-INT-003`, `GAP-INT-004`,
`GAP-INT-005`, `GAP-INT-008`, `GAP-INT-009`, `GAP-INT-011`, `GAP-ARC-001`,
`GAP-ARC-002`, and `GAP-ARC-003` — have no corresponding rule file anywhere
in the repository today.

**Where a value happens to collide with a real ID, the topics do not
match**, which is worse than a non-resolving reference because it is silent
until checked. Two examples:

| Gap entry | Registry `ksi_ids` | Registry subject | What that ID actually is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GAP-ARC-004` — Defender for Servers telemetry (SI-3/SI-4/IR-5) | `KSI-015`, `KSI-016` | Security-telemetry compensating control | `KSI-015` = *Supply Chain Risk Mitigation*, `KSI-016` = *Supply Chain Monitoring* (KSI-SCR theme) |
| `GAP-INT-006` — Expedited Windows Quality Updates (SI-2/RA-5) | `KSI-028`, `KSI-029` | Patch-SLA compensating control | `KSI-028` = *Recovery Objective Review*, `KSI-029` = *Recovery Capability Testing* (KSI-RPL theme, CP-family) |

Both `GAP-ARC-004` and `GAP-INT-006` are flagged `P1` in the registry —
`GAP-ARC-004` is explicitly `GAP_UNMITIGATED` and requires AO risk
acceptance. An assessor pulling the cited KSI ID to check the evidence trail
would land on an unrelated recovery-planning or supply-chain rule, not on
anything about Defender telemetry or patch SLAs.

**One entry does resolve correctly — into the *other* namespace.**
`GAP-ENT-001` (PIM-for-Groups password-reset escalation, a `DRIFT-AUTHZ`
rather than `DRIFT-BOUNDARY` finding) cites `ksi_ids: ["KSI-AC-02",
"KSI-AC-06", "KSI-AU-06"]`. These resolve exactly, by title, against
`rules/ksi/index.yaml`: `KSI-AC-02` = *Account Management*,
`KSI-AC-06` = *Least Privilege*, `KSI-AU-06` = *Audit Record Review,
Analysis, and Reporting* — a correct fit for a password-reset
privilege-escalation finding. This shows the registry's `ksi_ids` field is
not wrong by construction; it is inconsistently sourced. The most
recently-added entry (`GAP-ENT-001`) correctly cites the substrate-native
NIST-family namespace (§2's first corpus); the older Intune/Arc entries cite
numbers that resolve nowhere, or resolve to the wrong CR26-mapped rule.

**A fourth namespace exists and is disjoint from all of the above.**
`monitoring/ongoing_auth.py` — the OSCAL ongoing-authorization
evidence generator described in §6.4 below — reads
`docs/data/ksi-mappings.yml`, whose entries use a third ID *shape* entirely:
descriptive slugs (`KSI-IDENTITY-MFA`, `KSI-TELEMETRY-VISIBILITY`,
`KSI-NETWORK-SEGMENTATION`, `KSI-ENDPOINT-COMPLIANCE`, `KSI-DATA-PROTECTION`).
These map directly to NIST control IDs (`IA-2`, `AU-6`, `SC-7`, …) rather
than to either KSI corpus in §2, and are not cross-referenced from
`UIAO_137`, the gap registry, or either rule corpus.

**Net effect.** The substrate currently has four `KSI-`-prefixed ID spaces
in active use — the 191-rule NIST-family corpus, the 29-rule CR26-mapped
corpus, the boundary gap registry's ad hoc numbering, and the
ongoing-authorization generator's descriptive slugs — with exactly one
verified cross-reference between any pair of them (`GAP-ENT-001`, §5 above).
[UIAO_139 §2](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-gcc-moderate-realtime-boundary-impact.md)
already documents that the boundary series carries three unreconciled
*gap* registers "at different altitudes" and flags that as intentional,
tracked, non-blocking drift; this leaf's finding is the same category of
issue one level down, in the KSI IDs those registers cite, and it has not
previously been named. Given the gap registry's own header claims ATO
status (*"feeds SSP Section 13"*), reconciling or removing the non-resolving
`ksi_ids` values before that registry is submitted in an SSP package is
the concrete action item this leaf adds to the reconciliation backlog.

## 6. The Compensating-Control Pipeline — Detect, Register, Compensate, Evidence, Transport

The code that implements everything B.1/B.1.1/B.1.3 describe in narrative
form is a five-stage pipeline. Each stage is a real, running component;
none of this is aspirational.

### 6.1 Detect — `DRIFT-BOUNDARY` and the GCC Boundary Probe

ADR-033 adds `DRIFT-BOUNDARY` as a sixth drift class alongside
DRIFT-SCHEMA, DRIFT-SEMANTIC, DRIFT-PROVENANCE, DRIFT-AUTHZ, and
DRIFT-IDENTITY, defined as:

> *"A feature, capability, or service that is nominally within the
> authorized system boundary and appears available in administrative
> interfaces, but is functionally unavailable or produces no data due to
> undocumented restrictions, telemetry dependencies that conflict with
> FedRAMP compliance controls, or cloud service provider limitations not
> reflected in official documentation."*

with a severity table (security-control impact → P1; operational
visibility / compliance documentation → P2; feature capability / reporting
→ P3).

`adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/probe.py` implements the
detector. `GraphProbe` and `ARCProbe` issue live calls against Microsoft
Graph and Azure Resource Manager and classify the result into the six-value
status enum from ADR-033 (`FUNCTIONAL`, `SILENTLY_BLOCKED`,
`EXPLICITLY_UNAVAIL`, `PLANNING_PHASE`, `COMPENSATED`, `GAP_UNMITIGATED`).
The Endpoint Analytics probe is illustrative of the pattern:

```python
async def probe_endpoint_analytics_available(self) -> tuple[str, str]:
    # First: does the tenant have enrolled devices at all?
    status, devices = await self._get(".../deviceManagement/managedDevices?$count=true&$top=1")
    if devices.get("@odata.count", 0) == 0:
        return "PROBE_SKIPPED", "No enrolled devices to probe against"

    # Then: does the analytics endpoint return actual insights, or an empty shell?
    status2, scores = await self._get(".../beta/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsOverview")
    if status2 == 200 and not scores.get("insights", []):
        return "SILENTLY_BLOCKED", (
            "Endpoint analytics API responds but returns no insights. "
            "DiagTrack telemetry pipeline likely blocked by FedRAMP controls."
        )
```

The probe's `_build_finding()` also bridges each finding to the signal-level
telemetry-gaps SSOT (`gcc-moderate-telemetry-gaps.yaml`) via a
`telemetry_gap_refs` list, resolving to the exact `fixes` /
`partial-substitute` / `partial-bounded` / `not-fixed` rebuild verdict from
[B.1.3 §6.1](B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd#61-complete-fix-coverage-matrix-all-26-gap-rows)
via `load_rebuild_verdicts()`. A single probe run therefore emits, per
finding: the live functional status, the NIST controls it constrains, the
KSI IDs it should (per §5, does not always) affect, and the B.1.3 rebuild
verdict — one object serving three separate registers.

### 6.2 Register — the Compensating Controls Registry

`gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml` is the canonical, machine-generated
inventory the probe writes to. Its own header declares its authority
directly:

```yaml
# Canon ref:    ADR-033, Appendix U (extended)
# ATO artifact: yes — feeds SSP Section 13 (Inherited Controls)
# Generated by: gcc-boundary-probe-v1
# Update cycle: Weekly automated probe + governed PR on change
```

Walking one entry end to end shows the full contract the registry commits
to (`GAP-INT-001`, Endpoint Analytics):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `nist_controls` | `SI-4`, `SI-2` |
| `compensating_control` | a registered ID naming the in-boundary telemetry component (§6.3) |
| `status` | `COMPENSATED` |
| `ksi_ids` | `KSI-SI-04`, `KSI-SI-02` *(corrected 2026-08-06 — see §5)* |
| `ato_note` | *(paraphrased)* the SSP must not claim Endpoint Analytics as a functioning SI-4 implementation, and must instead document the in-boundary telemetry component (§6.3) as the compensating control |

The `ato_note` field exists specifically to prevent SSP overclaiming — it is
the registry's own guard against the exact failure mode ADR-033's
"Context" section describes: an SSP claiming an inherited Microsoft control
that is, in practice, non-functional in GCC-Moderate.

As of the current registry snapshot (post-2026-08-06 reconciliation, §5):
**17 gaps** tracked, **13 compensated**,
**3 unmitigated**, of which two are `P1` and carry explicit AO
risk-acceptance requirements — `GAP-INT-008` (Windows Device Health
Attestation, no compensating control, called out in its own `ato_note` as
*"the most significant security control gap in the GCC-Moderate Intune
deployment"*) and `GAP-ARC-004` (Defender for Servers telemetry — a
compensating control is named in the registry but the gap's `status` stays
`GAP_UNMITIGATED` pending verification; its `ksi_ids` were corrected in §5's
reconciliation). One entry (`GAP-ENT-001`) is structurally different
from the other sixteen: it is a `DRIFT-AUTHZ` detection gap (the underlying
Entra feature works; the upstream SCuBA baseline check `MS.AAD.7.4v1` does
not flag the specific PIM-for-Groups escalation path — tracked upstream at
`cisagov/ScubaGear#2072`), not a `DRIFT-BOUNDARY` telemetry gap, riding in
the same file because both are compensating-control entries feeding the
same SSP section.

### 6.3 Compensate — In-Boundary Telemetry Aggregation

`adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/telemetry.py`
implements the compensating control the registry assigns to the Intune
Endpoint-Analytics and Arc-telemetry gaps (§6.2). Its module docstring
states the mechanism directly:

> *"Collects device health telemetry within the FedRAMP boundary using
> Graph API management plane (not telemetry plane)... These are management
> API calls, not telemetry streams. They do not require DiagTrack or
> commercial telemetry endpoints."*

Two collection paths, both staying inside the boundary by construction —
the same "destination, not the data" principle
[B.1.3 §2](B1-3-rebuilding-boundary-blocked-analytics.qmd#2-the-in-boundary-principle--why-this-is-lawful-where-inheritance-is-not)
argues for the agency-scale rebuild, implemented here at the tenant-admin
scale:

- **`collect_intune_device_health()`** — paginates
  `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` via Graph, a management-plane
  endpoint available in every sovereign cloud (`cloud="commercial"`,
  `"gcc-high"`, or `"dod"`; commercial also serves GCC-Moderate per
  ADR-033). Populates a `DeviceHealthRecord` (compliance state, disk
  health, memory, boot time, TPM presence, OrgPath, Entra join state)
  tagged with a fixed data-source marker identifying it as substrate-
  collected, in-boundary telemetry rather than a Microsoft
  telemetry-pipeline artifact.
- **`collect_local_wmi_health()`** — runs a local PowerShell/CIM script
  (`Win32_ComputerSystem`, `Win32_OperatingSystem`, `Win32_LogicalDisk`,
  `Win32_Tpm`) with **no external network call at all**. Used for
  ARC-enrolled servers where `GAP-ARC-001`/`002`/`003` show Azure Monitor's
  telemetry endpoints blocked.

The module docstring's compliance claim is explicit and testable: *"Maps to
NIST 800-137 continuous monitoring requirements."* That is the standard
this component exists to satisfy without touching the commercial telemetry
pipeline SI-4/AU-2/AU-3/SC-7 constrain.

### 6.4 Evidence — OSCAL Ongoing Authorization

`monitoring/ongoing_auth.py`'s `OngoingAuthGenerator` is the
component that turns the registry and telemetry above into a FedRAMP
20x-consumable artifact. It loads `monitoring-sources.yml` (signal →
control) and `ksi-mappings.yml` (KSI → controls, evidence source — the
fourth namespace flagged in §5), and emits one OSCAL `observation` per
signal, each tagged with `control-id`, `signal`, and `evidence-source`
props under the `fedramp.gov/ns/oscal` namespace:

```python
def _build_observation(self, control_id, signal, description, evidence_source, source_system):
    return {
        "uuid": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "title": f"ConMon Evidence: {control_id} via {source_system}",
        "props": [
            {"name": "control-id", "value": control_id, "ns": "https://fedramp.gov/ns/oscal"},
            {"name": "signal", "value": signal, "ns": "https://fedramp.gov/ns/oscal"},
            {"name": "evidence-source", "value": evidence_source, "ns": "https://fedramp.gov/ns/oscal"},
        ],
        "methods": ["AUTOMATED"],
        "collected": now,
    }
```

The module docstring cites the exact requirement this satisfies: *"the
FedRAMP 20x Phase 2 ConMon requirement for machine-readable control
evidence,"* and the internal rule it enforces: *"ALWAYS cross-reference
every monitored control to an OSCAL evidence record."* `generate()`
produces a complete `ongoing-authorization` OSCAL document with
`impact-level: moderate` and an `import-ssp` reference — the artifact a
3PAO would consume directly during a ConMon review.

### 6.5 Transport (gated) — Reporting Egress

Evidence generation is not the same as evidence transmission, and the
substrate keeps them as two separate actuators. `reporting_egress`
is the gated transport leg — the only code path in the substrate that can
move a generated evidence artifact to an external federal destination.
Every submission passes through one gate table (`engine.submit`):

| Condition | Disposition | Transmits? |
|---|---|---|
| `live=False` (default) | `PLANNED` | no — dry-run only |
| `live=True`, no/invalid approval | `BLOCKED` | no — the L3 gate |
| `live=True` + approval, driver unconfigured | `BLOCKED` | no |
| `live=True` + approval + configured + valid | `SUBMITTED` | **yes — the only path** |

There is no code path that transmits without both `live=True` and a valid
`Approval` token — no autonomous (L4) submission at Moderate. And per
ADR-066, `CLAW` is deliberately not a configured destination in this
package: raw telemetry stays on the native pipe, consistent with the CLAW
corollary in
[B.1.1 §2.4](B1-1-gcc-moderate-three-way-conflict.qmd#24-the-claw-corollary--telemetry-sharing-does-not-resolve-any-corner) —
exporting evidence to CISA does not, and is not designed to, substitute for
the in-boundary compensating controls §6.1–6.4 build.

## 7. Cross-Reference: Registry Gap → NIST Control → Compensating Control → KSI (Corrected)

**As of the 2026-08-06 reconciliation (§5), this table is no longer
illustrative — it is what `gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml` now says.**
For the four entries below, the registry's `ksi_ids` field was corrected
to the mapping already derivable from each gap's own `nist_controls`
field, resolved against `rules/ksi/`. The same correction was applied to
every other non-resolving entry in the registry (§5); these four are
shown because they were §5's worked examples.

| Gap | NIST controls | Compensating control | Correct KSI reference (§2 namespace) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GAP-INT-001` Endpoint Analytics | SI-4, SI-2 | in-boundary telemetry component (§6.3) | `KSI-SI-04` (System Monitoring), `KSI-SI-02` (Flaw Remediation) — `rules/ksi/` |
| `GAP-ARC-004` Defender for Servers | SI-3, SI-4, IR-5 | proposed telemetry component, not yet effective (`GAP_UNMITIGATED`) | `KSI-SI-03`, `KSI-SI-04`, `KSI-IR-05` — `rules/ksi/` |
| `GAP-INT-008` Device Health Attestation | SI-7, IA-3 | none (`GAP_UNMITIGATED`) | `KSI-SI-07`, `KSI-IA-03` — `rules/ksi/` |
| `GAP-ENT-001` PIM password-reset escalation | AC-2, AC-6, AU-6 | PIM-escalation detection classifier (§6.2) | `KSI-AC-02`, `KSI-AC-06`, `KSI-AU-06` — already correct |

## 8. What This Leaf Is and Is Not

It **is** the control-ID and source-code companion to B.1/B.1.1/B.1.3: for
every compensating control the parent leaves describe in narrative terms,
this leaf names the file, the function, and the exact NIST/KSI identifiers
involved. It **is** an honest status report on the reconciliation state of
the substrate's own KSI and gap-registry artifacts, current as of this
leaf's `updated-at` date — §4 and §5 are findings, not settled state, and
will go stale themselves as the corpus keeps growing (§4 is itself an
instance of the failure mode it describes, and this leaf's numbers should
be re-verified against the live rule count at each `lifecycle_review`).

It **is not** a claim that the four KSI ID spaces named in §5 have been, or
need to be, merged into one. `UIAO_137 §1` explicitly scopes CR26-tailoring
and cross-corpus unification as separate work; this leaf's contribution is
naming the specific unresolved references so that work has a concrete
starting list rather than a general awareness that "the registers aren't
unified yet."

## 10. Provenance

This leaf was authored to close a gap identified during a review of the
boundary series against a direct question about NIST-control and FedRAMP-KSI
impact: B.1/B.1.1/B.1.3 answer at the mandate and pillar level but do not
name control IDs or code. Its content is derived from direct inspection of
`UIAO_137`, `ADR-033`, `gcc-boundary-gap-registry.yaml`, the
`gcc_boundary_probe` adapter source, `reporting_egress`, and
`ongoing_auth.py` as committed in this repository as of 2026-08-06, not from
the external source memo the other B.1.x leaves derive from. §4 and §5 are
net-new findings not previously recorded in any canon document; they should
be triaged into the same governance workflow that tracks
[UIAO_139 §2](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-gcc-moderate-realtime-boundary-impact.md)'s
three-registers note.
